title: Gateway Integration Sync — Embroider Customer Onramp (Week of 2028-04-29)
content:
Meeting: Integration Gateway Sync — Embroider customer onramp
Date: 2028-04-29 10:00 PDT (30m)
Attendees: Marissa Chen (lead SE), Ethan Brooks (field eng), Priya Nair (SRE oncall), Samir Patel (integration eng), Lena Martinez (CS), Diego Alvarez (customer success TPM)
Slack thread: #se-embroider (link above)
Objective: Weekly pulse to capture current integration status, surface blockers that could delay go-live, and align on next-week priorities. Short, tactical — keep action items small and owner-assigned.

Customer context (quick):
- Embroider is migrating their chat assistant to Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering + private control plane. Goal: staged rollout to 5% of traffic by 2028-05-10 and full cutover by 2028-05-31.
- Primary KPIs: median generation latency < 180ms, cost per 1k tokens <= $1.90, no PII exfil.
- Legal/compliance requested audit log retention at 13 months (currently 12m default).

High-level status summary:
- Infrastructure: VPC peering and customer firewall rules validated by NetOps; e2 nodes provisioned in eu-west-2 and us-west-2.
- Runtime: Canary model (rw-4-quant) onboarded and pinned to tag v2028-04-18; small perf regression observed at seq_len 2048 in eu-west-2.
- Routing/traffic: Canary route created; rollout plan approved but gating on perf SLA in eu-west-2.
- Security/compliance: KMS integration pending final legal signoff for key rotation policy; audit retention change under review.

Current progress by area:
- Network & infra (Ethan): VPC peering complete for both regions. Remaining: static NAT rule for customer egress (blocked on firewall ACL update, NetOps ticket NET-887).
- Serving runtime (Samir): Model quantization patch merged (PR infra#2148). Observed token-per-second drop ~8% on long-seq workloads in eu-west-2 after patch. Hypothesis: kernel selection fallback to slower kernel for that hardware.
- Observability (Priya): Traces and token-level cost hooks enabled; tracing shows increased KV cache misses on eu-west-2 canary nodes.
- Customer validation (Lena + Diego): Customer engineer ran smoke tests; chat payloads and function-calls work end-to-end but intermittent 502s during burst.

Blockers / Risks (ranked):
1) Performance regression in eu-west-2 (high) — effect: blocks canary rollout. Root cause likely kernel fallback or CPU scheduling. Action: run microbench with kernel telemetry. Owner: Samir. Due: 2028-05-01.
2) Firewall ACL update (medium) — NetOps queue causing NAT rule delay; prevents load testing from customer's staging CIDRs. Owner: Ethan / NetOps. Ticket: NET-887. Due: 2028-05-02.
3) KMS/key rotation policy (medium) — legal signoff needed; customer requires 90-day rotation and HSM-backed keys. Owner: Marissa / Legal. Linked artifact: CON-1121. Due: 2028-05-05.
4) Audit retention extension (low) — engineering needs config change and storage sizing estimate. Owner: Priya. Due: 2028-05-07.
5) Intermittent 502s under burst (medium) — likely autoscaler config + burst queue exhaustion. Owner: Samir + Priya. Due: 2028-05-03.

Action items (concrete):
- Samir: Run targeted microbench on eu-west-2 with kernel/CPU affinity logs, compare rw-4-quant baseline vs post-PR. Output: perf diffs and candidate mitigation (kernel override or smaller batch). Due 2028-05-01. Linked: infra#2148.
- Ethan: Escalate NET-887 with NetOps SRE and confirm ACL window; aim to unblock customer load tests. Due 2028-05-02.
- Marissa: Sync with Legal on KMS/hsm requirement, provide proposed exception path if rotation cadence conflicts with infra rollout. Due 2028-05-05.
- Priya: Provide storage sizing + cost delta for 13-month audit retention and PR to config repo. Due 2028-05-07.
- Lena + Diego: Collect 3 representative failing request traces and share in Confluence space; capture customer-side firewall logs. Due 2028-05-02.
- Samir+Priya: Triage 502 burst logs and adjust autoscaler target/queue limits; test with synthetic burst harness. Due 2028-05-03.

Decisions made this week:
- Rollout gating: proceed with us-west-2 canary if eu-west-2 regression persists. Rationale: us-west-2 results stable and gives staging traffic to validate end-to-end flow. Owner: Marissa.
- Batch-size rollback permitted for canary only: lower default batch from 32 -> 24 to reduce tail latency during bursts. Owner: Samir. To be toggled via runtime flag.

Notes-to-self / unresolved chatter (informal):
- Customer asked about per-route token caps; can patch with rate-limiter config but need product signoff on UI visibility. Slack note: @product-hosted-api FYI.
- Think about adding an explicit kernel-selection override knob to runtime for emergency fallbacks (short-term mitigation).
- Reminder: update the onramp runbook with new NAT troubleshooting steps (Ethan).

Follow-ups for next sync (2028-05-06):
- Perf microbench results and recommendation (Samir).
- NetOps ACL status (Ethan).
- Legal signoff or approved exception for KMS rotation (Marissa).
- 502 triage outcome and autoscaler tuning (Priya + Samir).
- Customer acceptance testing window confirmation (Lena + Diego).

Appendix (links & references):
- Jira: INT-4321 (Embroider onramp epic), NET-887 (NetOps ACL), CON-1121 (KMS/legal).
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Embroider+Onramp+Runbook
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2148 (quantization/kernel selection change)
- Synthetic test harness: https://internal.redwood.ai/tests/embroidery-burst-harness

Timestamped notes (raw):
- 2028-04-27 09:14 PDT — Samir: "saw a kernel fallback on the batch loop; trying kernel pin."
- 2028-04-28 14:02 PDT — Ethan: "NetOps asked for exact source CIDR, provided; waiting for window."
- 2028-04-29 08:03 PDT — Priya: "observability: KV cache misses spike at t+1s after cold start; added cache-warmup script to run in preflight."

End of notes.
Prepared by: Marissa Chen (solutions engineering)
Reviewed: 2028-04-30 by Samir Patel (integration eng)
